problem: The stated workload rate is impossible with the stated costs. 1,000,000 operations per second at 2 μs each needs 2 seconds of hypervisor time in every second of real time, so a student who multiplies will get an answer above 100% CPU. The rate is also never used, since the example then asks about 1,000 operations.
fix: Drop the per-second figure, or make it consistent: 'A workload performs privileged operations continuously; take 1,000 of them for this calculation.' If a rate is wanted, use one such as 100,000 operations per second, which costs 0.2 s of trap time per second under full virtualization.

problem: The definition covers only one half of the standard meaning. A sensitive instruction is one that either depends on machine state or changes machine state/configuration. As written, instructions whose effect alters the machine (halting the CPU, writing the page-table base register) fit only loosely, even though the chapter's own examples are of that kind.
fix: A sensitive instruction is one whose behaviour depends on the machine state, or which changes that state — the privilege mode, the interrupt flag, the page-table base register, the CPU halted state.

where: Section 3, table row 'Runs any OS image'
problem: 'Yes' is too broad: full virtualization runs any unmodified image built for the same CPU architecture, not literally any OS image (x86 will not boot an ARM kernel).
fix: Say 'Yes, any unmodified image for the same CPU architecture' in the full-virtualization column.
